$comment: The front-matter primitive (ADR-0795, ADR-0796, ADR-0797): every case with its exact output. Read by packages/definition/src/front-matter/front-matter.test.ts; a Rust twin reads the same file. `fields` is a list of [key, value] in file order, or null for a file outside the grammar. A merge's `later` names the side that wrote later.

parse.name: a note with three fields and a body
parse.text:
---
title: "Call dentist"
done: false
tags: ["health"]
---
Ask about the Thursday slot.

parse.name: an empty front matter
no opening fence: all body
an empty file: all body
only an opening fence: all body
no closing fence: all body
an unquoted string value: all body
a key written twice: all body
a comment line: all body
an indented YAML list: all body
a blank line between the fences: all body
a key without the space after its colon: all body
a key that starts with a digit: all body
a quoted key: all body
a byte-order mark before the fence: all body
a trailing comment after the value: all body
CRLF line endings
a closing fence at the end of the file
nested values, null, numbers, and an escaped newline
